The exact falsifiable next step is: a second evaluator, written from the public schema by an author with no access to knowledge_ledger/transaction.py, must reproduce the same conclusion for all 176,120 exhaustive worlds. Any disagreement on any world rejects the shared assumption.
claimAllowed: Within the declared bounds, the reference evaluator did not allow a recorded copy to change evidential mass, and did not allow an incomplete search to yield an absence conclusion. This is conformance behaviour in a frozen synthetic model.
claimNotAllowed: That the dual ledger recovers truth, that declared roots are genuinely independent, that the invariants hold outside the declared bounds, that any real-world evidence process is improved, or that KL-000 constitutes a knowledge transaction, a cross-system result, or any part of a First Transmission.
quantitativeCaveat: 75.7% of randomized worlds fail closed and produce no receipt, so eight of the ten invariants were exercised on 243,381 randomized worlds rather than 1,000,000. See results/kl000-effective-sample.json. The 95% rule-of-three upper bound for those eight is 1.23e-5 per receipt-producing world, not 3.0e-6.
knownLimits: ADV-001 high: an under-declared search space is undetectable, and the declaring party is the reporting party
ADV-002: one compromised issuer can mint unlimited roots
ADV-003: one appended conflicting record renders a whole transaction unevaluable
ADV-004: root identity is byte identity; no normalisation is specified
ADV-005: shared upstream dependency between roots is not representable
ADV-006: no issuer authentication; forged or replayed roots are indistinguishable
ADV-007: the claim proposition is free text and is never checked against the ledgers
